featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Gomuntak Restaurant and tried a variety of their thalis — chicken thali, surmai thali, prawns thali, and bangda thali.

The service was quick, which is a plus. The food was decent overall, but the spice level was quite mild. When it comes to fish dishes, a slightly higher spice level is usually expected, so that was a bit disappointing. The fish quality was okay, nothing exceptional.

On the brighter side, I personally liked their wade and the gravy, which stood out more than the main dishes. We also tried prawns lollipop, which was okay.

Overall, a decent place with fast service, but could be better if the flavors were a bit more bold.

customer_updates.text:
The restaurant serves authentic Maharashtrian cuisine, and it was an outstanding experience. We started with Agri Matka and Chulivarcha Chicken, both of which were bursting with flavor. The Agri Matka had that traditional rustic touch, slow-cooked to perfection, while the Chulivarcha Chicken, prepared on a traditional clay stove, was smoky, tender, and incredibly delicious.

For starters, we tried the Prawn Sukka, which was a perfect blend of spices, with succulent prawns cooked in a dry, aromatic masala. It was the ideal start to the meal. We also couldn't resist the Prawn Biryani, which was fragrant and loaded with juicy prawns. The balance of spices and flavors in every dish was just spot on.
Overall, this restaurant is a must-visit for anyone craving authentic Maharashtrian food. Every dish was prepared with care, and the flavors stayed true to the region's culinary heritage. I can't wait to go back and try more!

We visit Acharekar’s Malvan Katta, Dadar West at least once every year, and the best thing is they have maintained the same authentic taste and quality throughout the years.

Their food feels truly home-style and authentic Malvani, without unnecessary spice or heavy masala. Everything tastes fresh, balanced, and comforting.

We have tried Prawns Pulao, Chicken Kurkure, Mackerel Fry, Surmai Fry, Prawns Fry, Stuffed Pomfret, Bombil Fry and Solkadhi. every dish was excellent and perfectly cooked. Their Amboli is unbelievably soft and goes perfectly with the seafood and chicken dishes.

Even the chicken thali was amazing including the chicken gravy, chicken dry, and egg bhurji with rice, chapati, or bhakri.

If you want authentic Malvani food with consistent taste and homely preparation, this place is definitely worth visiting again and again.

​If you are looking for authentic Malvani food that genuinely feels like it was cooked with love, Acharekar's Malvan Katta is the absolute place to be. We had an incredible meal here, and every single dish managed to blow us away.
​Here is a breakdown of what we ordered:
​The OG Crab Lollipop: This was an absolute standout! We liked it so much that we couldn't resist ordering a second plate to take home with us. It's a must-try.
​Surmai Tawa Fry: The fish was incredibly fresh, perfectly spiced, and the portion size was massive—way more than I expected and absolutely worth it.
​Amboli & Mutton Sukka: My husband ordered this combo and was raving about it. According to him, the Mutton Sukka was just awesome, paired perfectly with the soft, fluffy amboli.
​Prawns Pulao: I ended the meal with this, and it was simply out of this world. The flavors were spot-on and packed with delicious coastal comfort.
​The warmth in the food really shows. Between the generous portions, the fantastic coastal flavors, and the hospitality, we are already planning our next visit.
Sorry forgot to take photos as I was busy digging in the food 😜
​Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Sankar Kasirajan
featured_reviews.review_text:
It was my daughter's birthday eve, and after some gentle persuasion to choose Pallavi's boutique café over Mumbai stalwarts like Trishna or Mahesh, we were seated in this beautifully done-up spot near Dadar's Shivaji Park. Though small, the space possesses a premium, fine-dining ambiance.

The Feast
Despite claiming to be "light eaters" (ahem!), we indulged in a vast selection, and every single dish was amazing. The true "Flavours" of Malwan shone through, outperforming many other seafood restaurants I've visited over the past 28 years (including Gajalee, Mahesh Lunch Home, and Sindhudurg).
Our order included:
	Refreshing Drinks: Sol Kadi, Kokum Soda, and Lemon Soda.
	Signature Seafood: Chutney Stuffed Pomfret Fry with Prawns, Chutney Stuffed Bombil Roll with Prawns, Sukka Crab, Tisrya Sukka, and Prawn Curry, paired with Rice Bhakri.
	Desserts: Ukdiche Modak and Puran Poli.

The Unforgettable Star
While every item was a feast for the taste buds, the Sukka Crab was the undisputed champion—absolutely outstanding! We literally wiped the plates clean and even drank the leftover Prawn Curry. This is food made with passion; food that truly leaves a lasting memory.

My words and photos simply cannot do full justice to the culinary magic at "Flavours of Malwan."

Don't just read about it—experience the authentic, soulful taste of Malwani cuisine for yourself!

Having visited countless seafood restaurants across Goa, the Konkan region, and Mumbai, I can confidently say that Jai Hind tops my list.

Yes, there’s almost always a long waiting line, and at times you may be asked to share a table with other diners. But honestly, that’s only because the place is packed with people who keep coming back for the food. And once you taste it, you’ll understand why.

Unlike many places that charge extra for every little thing, the thali here is genuinely generous and unlimited, you can ask for refills of the items in your thali as many times as you’d like.

Great food, excellent portions, and prices that feel justified. If you’re a seafood lover, the wait is absolutely worth it.

I recently visited Sachin Hotel, and I have to say, the quality has really gone downhill. It was a really bad experience. We ordered the pomfret fry thali, and honestly, it was a disaster… the quantity, quality, and taste were all disappointing. To make matters worse, we found a hair in the fish itself. We also tried the dal rice and chicken thali, but neither was great. When we informed the manager, he just said he’d give us another one. featured_reviews.name: Nagesh Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very disappointing experience during my recent visit. I ordered the chicken sukka thali, and unfortunately, almost everything about it was below expectations. The chicken was completely cold, even though the plate it was served on was hot, which was quite strange. The rest of the thali items, including the rice, were also cold and lacked freshness.

The taste was another major letdown- the chicken sukka was bland and tasteless, and the solkadi had a stale smell, making it unpleasant to consume. Overall, the food quality felt very poor.

Adding to the disappointment, the hygiene standards were questionable. Near the wash basin, I noticed empty liquor bottles in the dustbin placed alongside napkins and tissues, which gave a very unhygienic impression.

What makes this more upsetting is that I remember this hotel from 12-13 years ago as a place known for good taste and quality food. Sadly, the standards seem to have declined significantly. This visit turned out to be a really bad experience.

When those had finished the manager said they do not have upi only cash is allowed when they got angry and said they did not have cash, they gave them the upi code. So then they had come to us to say that the upi is not working before they they prepared the food. featured_reviews.name: sangeeta chaubal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Heard a lot about Hotel Sachin but wasn't really impressed with the whole experience.

The menu was vast and was confused with thali and special thali.

Place looked deserted and food was okay. The order taker clearly told us about some of the fish not being fresh  which seemed like a lie because he mentioned only pomfret which was expensive to be fresh. It was laughable.

We wanted to try out the mandeli fry which is something we don't try out daily but the waiter made sure that our taste buds don't matter and we had to order pomfret.

Food tasted bland especially the so called pomfret fry was horrible. It was bland and had no salt. Prawns masala was so-so.

Moreover when asked if the restaurant has a restroom, they say yes and guide us to a common toilet which is used by the whole building above and is just horrible. It is dirty and not women friendly at all.

Apart from this, I do order special mutton thali for my in-laws. The first thali that I ordered was impressive but when I ordered it the second time, it failed to deliver similar impression.

featured_reviews.name: Neha Save
featured_reviews.review_text:
Today I visited this place for the first time and  was thoroughly disappointed with my visit. The food was bland, and the Bombay ducks were especially shocking. They came with only a coating and no real flesh. To make matters worse, they weren’t served whole but sliced horizontally into two halves, stretched to look like a full piece. It felt like a deliberate attempt to mislead customers by giving the illusion of more fried pieces.

If you want to charge a higher price, that’s acceptable — but at least provide value for money. Sadly, this place failed on both taste and honesty. The service was equally pathetic, leaving me frustrated throughout the experience.

This was my first visit, and it will certainly be my last.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar Jondhale
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Malhar recently for lunch and ordered a variety of dishes, including Crab Lollipop, Prawns Koliwada, White Rice, Rava Bombil, and Agri-style Chicken Curry. We had also planned to try Amboli and Bhakri, but unfortunately, both were out of stock.

The Crab Lollipop and Prawns Koliwada were flavorful and well-prepared. However, the Agri-style Chicken Curry did not meet expectations. The use of garam masala was overpowering, and the excessive black pepper (kalimiri) affected the overall taste, though the dish was still edible.

The ambience of the restaurant was very beautiful, but I noticed some issues with cleanliness. For example, one of the glasses provided still had food particles stuck on the edge where a person drinks. I requested the steward to replace the glass; he took the dirty one but forgot to bring a new glass altogether, leaving me to drink directly from the bottle.

While the food was average overall, I was particularly disappointed with the service. Both the steward and the captain seemed uninterested and inattentive. Despite repeated requests, it took them over 15 minutes to bring tissues, even when asked clearly and politely.

Additionally, the Prawns Koliwada was served nearly 40 minutes later, after we had almost finished our main course. At that time, only 3–4 tables were occupied in the restaurant, so such a delay was unjustified. When I raised this issue with the captain, his casual response was, "Humare yaha thoda late hi hota hai." This type of attitude is not expected from a reputed establishment like Malhar.

In summary, although the ambience was nice and some dishes were good, the poor service, lack of attention to cleanliness, and indifferent staff attitude significantly impacted our overall dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Vijayshri
featured_reviews.review_text:
Khar Gymkhana, an iconic club founded in the late 1920s by a group of influential sports enthusiasts, has a rich history of nurturing talent and hosting prestigious tournaments. Over the decades, it has become a hub for a wide range of indoor and outdoor sports. The club offers excellent facilities for games like table tennis, billiards, cards, tennis, cricket, and swimming. In addition to the sports, Khar Gymkhana also boasts a popular restaurant called The Pavilion, known for its diverse menu of  food and drinks.

Membership to Khar Gymkhana is exclusive, with life membership available to individuals either within the immediate family or those married into a family that holds membership. There are also other types of memberships that can be obtained.

During our visit, we enjoyed a nice lunch and had time to observe some of the ongoing activities and games around the club. The food was delicious, and the service was surprisingly fast, considering the large crowd the restaurant was catering to. From the starters to the desserts, everything—whether vegetarian or non-vegetarian—was prepared well. However, there was one issue: the club lacked sufficient wheelchairs. A senior citizen in our group had to wait for a while to get access to one, as it was already in use by another member.
